source.title: Simply B1 Preliminary for Schools: 8 Complete Practice Tests
source.questions: Original student-book pages supplied by the user.
source.answerKey: WordHop-authored answer key and English explanations based on the supplied recordings; not a publisher key.

parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: How had the girl expected to travel?
questions.explanation: She originally expected to travel by rail, but the trains were cancelled. She eventually came by car; flying was only a suggestion.
questions.evidence: At first we had thought of coming by rail

questions.prompt: Which skirt did the girl buy?

optionText.A: A plain straight skirt with a belt.
optionText.B: A flared skirt with horizontal stripes.
optionText.C: A short denim skirt with buttons down the front.

questions.explanation: She bought the short striped skirt. The long belted skirt was uncomfortable, and she disliked the other skirt’s buttons.
questions.evidence: It’s got stripes.

questions.prompt: What is the weather forecast for Saturday?

optionText.A: Stormy weather, with rain and lightning.

questions.explanation: Saturday will be milder but still cloudy. The storm is forecast for Friday, and sunshine for Sunday.
questions.evidence: This will be followed by milder weather on Saturday. Still cloudy though.

questions.prompt: Which book has the boy already bought?

optionText.A: A book with a sailing ship on its cover.
optionText.B: A book with wild animals on its cover.
optionText.C: A book with mountains on its cover.

questions.explanation: He has already bought “Climbing Mount Everest,” matching the mountains on the cover. The animal and sailing books are still on order.
questions.evidence: I’ve already bought one called Climbing Mount Everest.

questions.prompt: Which lesson did the girl have first?
questions.explanation: She corrects herself and says maths came first, followed by science. Art was moved to the end because the teacher was delayed.
questions.evidence: Oh no. First we had maths and then science.

questions.prompt: Who is the girl phoning?
questions.explanation: She is calling about being late for a haircut. The dentist and chemist were earlier stops that delayed her.
questions.evidence: If I’m too late for a cut, I can re-book for the weekend

questions.prompt: What is the boy’s mother going to get?
questions.explanation: His mother will bring soft drinks home from work. Pizza and ice cream are already in the freezer.
questions.evidence: Now you need some soft drinks.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a new sports centre.

What does the girl say about it?

optionText.B: It’s worth becoming a full member.
optionText.C: Members pay extra for some classes.

questions.explanation: Full membership works out cheaper than paying registration and individual class fees. Her discount was a special student/new-member offer, not a discount for everybody.
questions.evidence: Without full membership, you have to pay a registration fee […] and then also pay for each class. So membership actually works out cheaper.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about shopping online.

How does the boy feel about it?

optionText.A: He finds it difficult to decide what to buy.

questions.explanation: He says he is generally happy with his online purchases and finds online shopping stress free. Difficulty deciding and anxiety refer to shopping in physical shops.
questions.evidence: Generally I’ve been happy with what I bought, so it works for me. Stress free shopping.

questions.prompt:
You will hear a girl telling a friend about a holiday she’s been on.

What does the girl say about herself and her cousin?

optionText.B: They enjoyed most of their time together.

questions.explanation: She and her cousin wanted different activities: she liked walking, while her cousin preferred reading and films. She would not repeat the holiday.
questions.evidence: We had different ideas about how to spend our days.

questions.prompt:
You will hear a boy asking a girl about an article he has written.

The girl tells the boy to
questions.explanation: The girl likes the topic and examples but says the article still contains spelling and grammar mistakes. Those need correcting before submission.
questions.evidence: But it still has some spelling and grammatical mistakes.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a new television series.

What does the boy think about it?
questions.explanation: Although the series has weaknesses, it makes him laugh. He criticises the acting rather than praising it.
questions.evidence: Despite all that, it makes me laugh

questions.prompt:
You will hear a girl talking about a new teacher.

How do the girl’s parents feel?

optionText.A: negative towards her new maths teacher
optionText.C: surprised by her progress in maths

questions.explanation: Her parents are amazed by her improvement in maths and grateful to the new teacher. The possible class change concerns her friend.
questions.evidence: My parents are amazed as they had given up with my maths. They feel grateful to him.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time.
parts.heading: Radio Presenter
parts.context: You will hear a man called Jack Pindar talking to a group of students about his job as a radio presenter.

questions.prompt: At university Jack studied ________.
questions.explanation: He studied history at university, despite doing DJ work and loving music.
questions.evidence: In fact, I was a history student

questions.prompt: Before the show Jack drinks ________.
questions.explanation: He drinks a large cup of tea before presenting. Coffee is what others drink, and juice comes after the show.
questions.evidence: Everyone eats and drinks loads of strong coffee, but I’m a tea man myself. One big cup

questions.prompt: Jack’s favourite part of the job is ________.
questions.explanation: Doing interviews is his favourite part of the job because he meets interesting people. The plural “interviews” matches the activity he describes.
questions.evidence: The best thing of all is when I get to do interviews.

questions.prompt: Jack was embarrassed when he couldn’t remember a ________.
questions.explanation: He once forgot a politician’s name during an interview. He specifically rules out forgetting dates and times.
questions.evidence: Once in the middle of talking to a politician, I forgot their name.

questions.prompt: If Jack wasn’t a radio presenter he would be a ________.
questions.explanation: He would now choose to be a reporter because he enjoys talking to people. Teaching and acting were earlier interests.
questions.evidence: If I changed careers now, I would definitely be a reporter

questions.prompt: Jack will be doing a charity show at ________ at the weekend.
questions.explanation: The charity event is at Hatfield House. He spells H-A-T-F-I-E-L-D, confirming the place name.
questions.evidence: The charity event I am doing at Hatfield House […] it’s spelled H A T F I E L D House.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear an interview with a 17-year-old boy called Daniel, who arranged some events to raise money to improve a local youth club.

questions.prompt: Daniel decided to try to raise money because

optionText.A: there was a lot of crime in his neighbourhood.
optionText.B: he and his friends were bored.
optionText.C: it was part of a school project.

questions.explanation: A school project to help local people prompted the fundraising. He says his village is peaceful and that the youth club prevents boredom.
questions.evidence: We have to do a project at school to help the local people and it seemed like a good idea.

questions.prompt: How did Daniel let people know about the events?

optionText.B: He put posters in public places.

questions.explanation: He set up a Facebook page and emailed people. Posters were not allowed, and phoning everyone was impractical.
questions.evidence: I emailed people and I set up a Facebook page to let everyone know about it.

questions.prompt: Daniel says that in the beginning he thought

optionText.B: it would be easy to raise the money.
optionText.C: it would take a long time to raise the money.

questions.explanation: He expected fundraising to take time, although he believed hard work would succeed. He did not expect easy or immediate results.
questions.evidence: I wasn’t expecting to have good results quickly.

questions.prompt: How did Daniel feel after the first event?
questions.explanation: The cooking competition attracted only ten entrants and raised less money than he expected. Eating cake cheered him up, but the fundraising result was disappointing.
questions.evidence: Only 10 people took part […] raised a disappointing amount of money.

questions.prompt: Daniel’s favourite event was
questions.explanation: The dog show was his favourite: it was fun, drew a crowd, and raised a lot. He was less excited by the Sunday sale.
questions.evidence: The dog show was really amazing […] it was brilliant fun.

questions.prompt: In the future, Daniel plans to
questions.explanation: He plans to raise money again for another useful local cause. The youth-club improvements are finished, and he does not want to take up cooking.
questions.evidence: I think I’ll probably start raising money again to do something useful for our town.
